transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-22
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Anika (Solutions), Daniel (Polaris Head of Data), Lisa (Security), Arjun (PM)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check on attendees?
[00:06] Daniel Kim: Yeah Daniel here, Lisa and Arjun are with me. Thanks, Maya.
[00:10] Lisa Wong: Hi — linked in chat.
[00:12] Carlos (Redwood SE): Carlos here on the SE side, I'll run through the Console demo and the backend bits.
[00:16] Maya: Great. Today we'll focus on request storage governance — how Redwood stores or doesn't store requests, redaction options, and how the Console and Redwood Optimize recommend settings for cost vs privacy.

Summary and opening Q:
[00:32] Arjun Mehta: High-level first — we need to know default behavior. If we flip anything on in the Console, will customer data be persisted? Are logs shipped to S3?
[00:40] Maya: Good question. By default in our hosted offering we retain request metadata for 30 days for operational debugging, but request bodies are not retained unless you opt in. For the demo I'll show the toggles — 'Store requests' is off by default for privacy-minded orgs.
[00:52] Lisa: Did you say 30 days metadata? We need to be careful — our compliance needs 90-day audit windows but we also have a policy to minimize stored PII.
[01:01] Carlos: Right, metadata retention is configurable. You can set retention windows per-project in the Console — 0, 7, 30, 90, or custom. Bodies and tokens have a separate toggle. Also, request logs can be scrubbed with redaction rules before storage.

Console walkthrough (live):
[01:22] Carlos: (screen shares) Ok here's the Console. Top nav: Projects -> Governance -> Request Storage. See the 'Request Storage' switch — it's currently OFF for this demo tenant.
[01:30] (static noise, mutter)
[01:32] Maya: Note — the switch off means zero request bodies are persisted. We still keep trace IDs and routes to help debugging, but we do not store prompt or response text.
[01:40] Daniel: If we had to enable storage for a pilot, can we do per-route? We only want to store logs for the reranker route and not the chat route.
[01:46] Carlos: Yes per-route toggles. You can also set a per-model override and environment (prod/staging). We'll show that — Route Table -> edit -> Storage Policy -> choose 'No body', 'Store redacted', 'Store full (not recommended)'.

[02:10] Lisa: How does redaction work? We have bank account numbers and PII in prompts.
[02:14] Carlos: Two modes: automatic PII heuristics and custom regex masks. Automatic uses ML heuristics to identify emails, SSNs, credit card numbers, phone numbers. You can choose action: mask, replace with [REDACTED], or drop the field. For highest assurance we also support a pre-processing webhook — you can run your own proxy to sanitize before it hits Redwood.
[02:35] Arjun: Does automatic redaction affect latency? We need tight SLAs.
[02:40] Carlos: Minimal — redaction is done asynchronously for storage paths. For sync paths we do a fast path masking (approx +5-15ms per request depending on length). For throughput sensitive routes we recommend Enable caching/prefix caching in Redwood Optimize and set storage to 'Store none'.

(Transcript noise — 'K V cache' vs 'KV cache')
[03:05] Daniel: You mentioned K V cache earlier — will caching conflict with privacy rules?
[03:09] Maya: Good point — KV cache is ephemeral in our runtime and never included in stored request bodies. Cache is in-memory on the serving node, not written to logs.

Legal & compliance specifics:
[03:22] Lisa: For GDPR/DSR (data subject requests), if someone asks for deletion, how do you reconcile requests that hit your logs?
[03:30] Carlos: If 'Store requests' is off, there's nothing to delete. If it's on, we have an export and delete API for stored requests — you can programmatically find and delete entries by trace-id or user-id. We also support filtered exports for legal review. Note that audit logs (who toggled settings) are retained in the control plane for 365 days by default under the policy tab.
[03:52] Lisa: KMS — we require envelope encryption with customer-managed keys. Is that possible?
[03:56] Maya: Yes. We integrate with customer KMSs — AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or bring-your-own HSM. Keys can be configured per-project; all stored request data is encrypted at rest with envelope encryption and the data keys are wrapped by your CMK. We'll share the KMS integration doc after the call.

Live demo: redaction rule editor
[04:20] Carlos: Opening the redaction editor — here's a sample rule: detect 16-digit numbers and replace with ****-masked. You can chain rules and add exceptions. There's also a 'preview' pane that runs sample payloads and shows masked output.
[04:38] (Lisa: okay, nice)
[04:40] Carlos: This preview uses a test sandbox dataset; in production you can attach a 'sample set' to validate rules before enabling them for storage.

Pilot mechanics & telemetry:
[04:55] Maya: For the pilot we recommend: keep Store Requests OFF by default; enable per-route 'Store redacted' for the 2 routes you need; enable automatic PII heuristics with mask action; enable encrypted-at-rest with customer KMS; set retention window to 30 days initially and move to 90 if needed.
[05:12] Arjun: How will we measure cost delta? If redaction runs, do we get charged extra?
[05:16] Carlos: Redaction itself is part of storage preprocessing — storage billing is for retained bytes and for additional re-processing jobs. For our unit economics, you pay for tokens served as usual plus storage bytes and optional export jobs. We'll show sample numbers: storing 1M requests with average 2KB saved as redacted will be X $/month — I'll run Polaris-specific numbers after you send sample payloads.

Questions from customer:
[05:42] Lisa: Is there any chance redacted data can be reconstructed or is it irreversible?
[05:46] Carlos: Masking is irreversible if you choose 'replace with [REDACTED]'. For 'hash' options, it's deterministically hashed — useful for deduping but considered pseudonymization, not deletion. If you need irreversible deletion we recommend 'drop field' or 'replace fixed token' modes.

[06:10] Daniel: About debugging—if request body isn't stored, how do we troubleshoot a bad model response?
[06:15] Maya: We support ephemeral replay with explicit opt-in: you can enable a short-lived 'debug store' for a session—bodies are stored for a configurable short TTL (e.g., 6 hours) and tagged 'debug' so they auto-delete. Access is RBAC-protected and audited.
[06:30] Arjun: RBAC — can we limit which roles can toggle storage or request exports?
[06:34] Carlos: Yes, RBAC is per-action. In the Console under Admin -> Roles you can create a 'Compliance Reader' role that can view redaction configs and exports but cannot toggle Store Requests. All admin actions write an audit event with user and timestamp.

(Short pause, someone types in chat)
[07:02] Maya: quick aside — there's also an API-level param to send a header 'redwood-store: never' that you can programmatically set per-request if you want dynamic control from your application. This is useful if you want to redact certain user-initiated actions.
[07:15] Lisa: That header — is it enforced server-side or can a client just not send it? We need server-side enforcement so engineers can't accidentally store PII.
[07:22] Carlos: It's enforced server-side against the project policy. The header is just a suggestion; project policy and RBAC are the source-of-truth.

Deep dive — KMS & key rotation:
[07:40] Lisa: What's rotation look like for wrapped keys? We have quarterly rotation.
[07:44] Anika (Solutions): Rotation is supported — we rewrap data keys with the new CMK and keep an immutable audit trail. Rotation can be scheduled and you can do immediate rotation via API. We'll include rotation guarantees in the security packet.

Optimize recommendations for cost/privacy tradeoffs: 
[08:05] Carlos: Redwood Optimize suggests batching windows and caching TTLs per-route. If you reduce synchronous response latency by 10ms, you might increase token cost by ~0.6% due to additional cache misses — Optimize will show predicted token cost delta when you change settings. It also recommends turning off storage for high throughput low-privacy routes.
[08:28] Arjun: Example — if we run reranker in Dedicated and store redacted logs, will Optimize still recommend batching?
[08:34] Carlos: Yes, Optimize is workload-aware and will consider storage policies as part of its suggestions; if storage is enabled it will weigh that into the cost model.

Audience misc — small transcription noise: "re-assign" -> "reassign"
[09:05] Daniel: Anything about removal requests downstream — if a user asks us to remove content and we've sent it to Redwood, how is provenance handled?
[09:12] Maya: We provide traceability — each request can be looked up by trace-id and you can delete or export it. For downstream systems (e.g., if you exported to SIEM) you'll need to run deletion there too; we can include export hooks that hang off deletion events so you can propagate deletes to other systems.

Timebox and recap:
[09:40] Maya: We're at the core of what you asked. Quick recap before we move to the action list — keep Store Requests OFF by default, use per-route 'Store redacted' for limited cases, use automatic heuristics + custom regex, enable KMS CMK, and pilot for 2 weeks.
[09:56] Lisa: That sounds reasonable — we want the pilot contract language to explicitly state that logs will be encrypted with our key and retention windows will be adjustable.
[10:05] Maya: We'll add that to the pilot SOW.

Closing Q&A and small tangents: 
[10:12] Arjun: Will data residency be a problem — can we restrict storage to EU locations only?
[10:16] Carlos: Yes, per-project region constraints exist. For hosted we store retained logs in the selected region; for Private deployments you control residency entirely.

[10:30] Lisa: Do you have SIEM connectors or Splunk forwarders?
[10:33] Maya: We have native export connectors to S3, GCS, and a Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) integration. Exports can be scheduled and filtered.

Wrap and next steps:
[11:00] Maya: Great — next steps as we covered: I'll send the security packet and a short GIF showing the retention toggle. Carlos will run the perf & cost estimate once you provide sample payloads. We'll schedule the security deep-dive with Lisa. Anything else?
[11:15] Lisa: Please include the legal redaction guarantees in writing — we'll review with procurement.
[11:20] Daniel: We'll get the sample payloads to Carlos by Monday.

End of call
[11:30] Maya: Thanks, everyone — we'll follow up.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard words ("K V cache" instead of KV cache), speaker short-hands, and a few overlapped words during rapid Q&A.
